detail:
The review found the budget was spent in two currencies: selection filled it with estimateTokens (chars/4) while annotateEmitted reported the conservative bound (~1 token/byte), and nothing compared them. That is fixed — selection, decisionTiers and the receipt now all use the declared tokenizer, and retrieval.token_usage.over_budget / omitted_decisions report truncation explicitly instead of the old "token_estimate approximately equals max_tokens" coincidence (whose documented heuristic had become false on every call; the tool description is updated).

THE CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly: a 4000-token budget now genuinely guarantees <= 4000 tokens, and buys roughly a quarter of the content it used to. Four existing tests had to be re-baselined for the unit change (two assembler budgets 30 -> ~150, a gap7 control 400 -> 1600, overhead thresholds 100/200 -> 400/800). The field's standing constraint is "do not make assemble quieter", which cuts the other way.

This is NOT inherent to the design — it is the price of the PROVEN table (1 token per UTF-8 byte). A calibrated table would put prose near 0.3 tokens/byte and the 4x would essentially vanish, restoring the old packing density while keeping the guarantee. scripts/calibrate-tokenizer.mjs and the corpus are ready; it needs one run with an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

So the tokenizer decision I escalated earlier is now load-bearing rather than cosmetic: ship proven (safe, 4x stingier briefings) or calibrate (same safety class, near-previous density). I did not pick unilaterally, and I did not fabricate ratios to make the number look better.
summary: Unifying the budget currency makes every 2.x briefing ~4x tighter for the same max_tokens — the visible cost of shipping an uncalibrated tokenizer table. Lead decision needed.
